Thought: In reverse-phase HPLC, retention time depends on the hydrophobicity of the molecule. More hydrophobic compounds interact more strongly with the stationary phase (which is non-polar) and have longer retention times. I need to understand how the pH change affects the hydrophobicity of salicylic acid.

Salicylic acid has a pKa of 2.75. This means:
- At pH 5 (which is > pKa), salicylic acid will be predominantly in its deprotonated form (salicylate anion). The negative charge makes it more hydrophilic.
- At pH 0 (which is << pKa), salicylic acid will be predominantly in its protonated (neutral) form. The neutral form is more hydrophobic than the charged form.

In RP-HPLC, more hydrophobic compounds have longer retention times because they interact more strongly with the non-polar stationary phase. Since lowering the pH from 5 to 0 converts salicylic acid from its more hydrophilic form (anion) to its more hydrophobic form (neutral), the retention time will increase.
Final Answer: [ANSWER]B[/ANSWER]
